\begin{document}
Let $\beta>0$ and let $\mu$ be a nonzero chemical potential.  We use the
following displayed convention for the lead occupation:
\begin{equation}
n_F(\omega) = \frac{1}{e^{\beta(\omega-\mu)}+1} .
\label{eq:shifted-occupation-definition}
\end{equation}
Particle-hole symmetry is then claimed as
\begin{equation}
n_F(-\omega) = 1-n_F(\omega) .
\label{eq:shifted-occupation-ph}
\end{equation}
\end{document}
